subject: Compact vs Core bundle — guidance for BrightEdge
messages:
From: Natalie Park <natalie.park@brightedge.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@brightedge.ai
Date: 2027-05-16T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Compact vs Core — quick guidance?

Hi Rishi,

We ran through the bundles in the proposal and had two internal camps: one prefers the Compact bundle for the immediate POC to save cost, the other wants Core so we don't have to rework prompts later. We're trying to avoid a long procurement loop. Can you help highlight the typical customer profiles who pick Compact vs Core, and any recommended upgrade path (credits, pro-rated, seat mapping) if we start small?

Attachments: pricing_grid.xlsx (xls)

Thanks,
Natalie
Head of Platform Engineering
BrightEdge

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>
To: Natalie Park <natalie.park@brightedge.ai>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-17T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact vs Core — quick guidance?

Hi Natalie — thanks for the note and for sharing the internal tradeoff. Short version: Compact is great for short-term evals or bursty workloads where cost matters most; Core is better when you expect steady production traffic and need feature parity (routing, KV-preservation, higher batch sizes).

I looped in Priyom and Marissa for how we usually handle upgrades without a procurement re-bid. Below are the considerations we typically call out:

- Migration friction: Compact often uses smaller capacity/quant profiles; moving to Core can require retraining prompt heuristics or a short regression pass.
- Credits & proration: We can apply unused committed credit toward a Core commit if you convert within 90 days; exact proration depends on the monthly cadence.
- Seat/throughput mapping: We translate Compact "seat" to Core capacity via a throughput multiplier (usually 1 Compact seat ~= 0.6 Core seat for token-heavy workloads).

If you can share expected monthly tokens and latency SLO, we can sketch a concrete mapping and potential discount ladder.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Natalie Park <natalie.park@brightedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-18T11:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact vs Core — quick guidance?

Hi both — quick tactical note from SE perspective:

1) If BrightEdge plans to keep under 200M tokens/month for the first 3 months, Compact + our optimizer rules (prefix cache + 3x batching window) will be materially cheaper and still satisfy 95th pctl latencies for interactive use.
2) For trial-to-prod conversion, we recommend a two-step rollout: a) reserve a small Core pool for canary (10% traffic) while keeping Compact for baseline, b) when quality/latency stable, shift traffic and convert Compact seats to Core via a 60-day credit conversion.
3) We can commit to a one-time upgrade credit (5-10% of committed spend) if the deal size is >$150k ARR to offset rework.

I'll attach a one-pager with cost delta examples; Marissa, does that match our current compensation/discount guidelines?

Thanks,
Priyom
Solutions Engineer

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Natalie Park <natalie.park@brightedge.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Compact vs Core — quick guidance?

Natalie — welcome, and good framing. A couple of policy notes on discounts and packaging:

- Discount ladder: we typically tier discounts by AIM (Annualized Implied Monthly) commit: 0-150k (none/standard), 150-500k (5-10%); >500k (12-18% with enterprise T&Cs). For upgrades, credits are capped at 10% unless legal approves a larger concession.
- Feature bundling: Core includes the routing + observability add-ons that Compact does not. If you need observability for the canary, you can add the observability module to Compact as an add-on for ~15% of the Core list price to avoid an immediate tier migration.
- Contracting: If procurement needs a clean path to upgrade without a new PO, we can include a conversion clause in the PO that allows seat re-mapping and credit rollover once during the 90-day window.

Happy to run numbers — Rishi, Priyom, can you send the token/latency estimates and I'll produce a short commercial sketch with two scenarios (start-compact + convert; start-core).

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Customer Success Manager

Natalie — looping back with the takeaway and next steps:

1) If you want to keep procurement quick: sign Compact + observability add-on, include the conversion clause, and use our 60-day canary approach. That minimizes upfront spend and gives us runway to measure regressions.
2) If your roadmap expects steady production (500M+ tokens/month within 6 months), start Core — we can discount 8-12% at the 12-month commit level and avoid rework.

Next step: can you share a projected token range (low/expected/high) and whether you need observability/trace retention? We'll produce a two-row commercial sketch and a PO-friendly conversion clause for your procurement team.

Best — happy to hop on a 20-min call if you prefer.

Rishi
